question: How many hydrogen atoms will be added along with one carbon atom in the next member of a homologous series?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A group of compounds with the **same general formula** but have **differences in the length of the carbon chain **are referred to as **homologous series**.
 
• A homologous series of compounds usually have **similar chemical and physical properties** because they share a **fixed set of functional groups**.
 
• The **next member **of a homologous series by a molecular formula of CH₄, **containing one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms**, constituting a **molecular mass of 14u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As **alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes only have carbon and hydrogen atoms**, they are also known as **hydrocarbyl groups**.
 
• The **kinds of bonds between the two carbon atoms, such as double or triple bonds**, in alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes are the **difference **between them.
 
• The **substituent atoms or groups of atoms that are joined to particular molecules to form functional groups.**. 
 
• A **molecule's behaviour and chemical reactions can be predicted in a systematic manner **if it has a functional group.
